rests on fact {id} with status rejected.what: The analysis uses fact {id}, but that fact was rejected.
rests on fact {id} with status rejected.why: It was withdrawn, a quote was not found in its saved source, or the checker judged that the quote does not support it.
rests on fact {id} with status rejected.do: Take {id} out of the analysis, or find a source that supports it and add it as a new fact.

rests on fact {id} with status proposed.what: The analysis uses fact {id}, but that fact has not been checked to the end.
rests on fact {id} with status proposed.why: Its quote check or its support check is still open.
rests on fact {id} with status proposed.do: Run the checks for {id} and settle the facts, or take {id} out of the analysis.

rests on fact {id} with status missing.what: The analysis uses fact {id}, but that fact does not exist.
rests on fact {id} with status missing.why: The number may be wrong, or the fact was never added.
rests on fact {id} with status missing.do: Correct the number, or add the fact and check it.

a text names fact {id} with status rejec.what: A text of the analysis names fact {id}, but that fact was rejected.
a text names fact {id} with status rejec.why: A reader would take the text as resting on a fact that did not hold up.
a text names fact {id} with status rejec.do: Take {id} out of the text, or rest the point on a fact that counts.

a text names fact {id} with status propo.what: A text of the analysis names fact {id}, but that fact has not been checked to the end.
a text names fact {id} with status propo.why: Its quote check or its support check is still open.
a text names fact {id} with status propo.do: Check {id} and settle the facts, or take it out of the text.

a text names fact {id} with status missi.what: A text of the analysis names fact {id}, but there is no such fact.
a text names fact {id} with status missi.why: The number may be wrong, or the fact was never added.
a text names fact {id} with status missi.do: Correct the number in the text, or take it out.

a text names fact {id} with status withd.what: A text of the analysis names fact {id}, but that fact was withdrawn.
a text names fact {id} with status withd.why: A withdrawn fact is kept so the reader sees it, and it is never relied on.
a text names fact {id} with status withd.do: Take {id} out of the text, or rest the point on a fact that counts.

a text names fact {id} with status.what: A text of the analysis names fact {id}, but that fact cannot be relied on.
a text names fact {id} with status.why: Only confirmed or uncertain facts may be named in the analysis.
a text names fact {id} with status.do: Take {id} out of the text, or check it until it is settled.

rests on fact {id}.what: The analysis uses fact {id}, but that fact cannot be used yet.
rests on fact {id}.why: Only confirmed or uncertain facts may be used in the analysis.
rests on fact {id}.do: Check {id} until it is settled, or take it out of the analysis.

quote not found in saved copy.what: The quote for {id} is not in the saved copy of its source word for word.
quote not found in saved copy.why: The quote was changed, shortened or written from memory, or the saved copy was changed afterwards.
quote not found in saved copy.do: Take the exact wording from the saved copy and add it as a new fact.

supporting quote not found in saved copy.what: A supporting quote for {id} is not in the saved copy of its source word for word.
supporting quote not found in saved copy.why: The quote was changed or written from memory, the source has no saved copy, or the copy was changed afterwards.
supporting quote not found in saved copy.do: Take the exact wording from the saved copy and add the fact again as a new fact.

reason does not follow from the checks.what: The reason given for the status of fact {id} does not match its checks.
reason does not follow from the checks.why: The reason was written or changed by hand after the facts were settled.
reason does not follow from the checks.do: Settle the facts again so that every reason follows from its checks.

the reasons for uncertain do not follow.what: The reasons recorded for fact {id} (why it is uncertain) do not match its checks.
the reasons for uncertain do not follow.why: The program works the reasons out when it settles the facts. They were changed by hand, or a source was marked as repeating another one since.
the reasons for uncertain do not follow.do: Settle the facts again so that the reasons follow from the checks.

saved copy has changed.what: The saved copy of source {id} is no longer the text that was saved.
saved copy has changed.why: The file was edited or replaced after it was saved.
saved copy has changed.do: Save the source again as a new source, add its facts again from the new copy, and take the old facts out of the analysis.

result does not match its inputs.what: A total in the analysis does not match the figures it is built from.
result does not match its inputs.why: The program computed {value} from the facts listed for it.
result does not match its inputs.do: Use the program's figure, or correct the list of facts the total is built from.

the earlier run has facts whose status n.what: The earlier run has facts whose status no longer matches their checks, so it cannot be compared yet.
the earlier run has facts whose status n.why: A fact there was withdrawn, given a new verdict or linked to another source, and its facts were not settled since.
the earlier run has facts whose status n.do: Settle the facts of the earlier run, then compare the two runs again.

the ignore file of a private run must ke.what: This private run is no longer kept out of the project's history.
the ignore file of a private run must ke.why: The line that keeps the whole run folder out of git is gone, so git could take in its non-public material.
the ignore file of a private run must ke.do: Put the single line * back into the run's .gitignore, with no line that starts with !, then check the run again.

a publishable report may not be built fr.what: This run was started in private mode, so no version of its report may be published.
a publishable report may not be built fr.why: A private run is for material that is not public, also when every source in it is public now.
a publishable report may not be built fr.do: For a version to publish, start a public run with the same question, without the documents.

a publishable report may use public sour.what: This run contains a source that is not public, so its report cannot be published.
a publishable report may use public sour.do: Build the report without the publishing option, or run the question again in public mode.

the comparison is out of date.what: The comparison with the earlier run no longer matches the facts of this run.
the comparison is out of date.why: Facts were added, settled again or withdrawn after the comparison was made.
the comparison is out of date.do: Run the comparison with the earlier run again.

the comparison was changed after it was.what: The comparison with the earlier run was changed after the program wrote it.
the comparison was changed after it was.why: It was edited by hand, or damaged.
the comparison was changed after it was.do: Run the comparison with the earlier run again.

a publishable report may not compare aga.what: This report compares against an earlier run that used sources that are not public.
a publishable report may not compare aga.why: The comparison shows values from that earlier run, which are confidential.
a publishable report may not compare aga.do: Build the report without the publishing option, or compare against an earlier public run instead.

analysis is missing.what: The analysis has not been written yet.
analysis is missing.why: A report needs the key messages and their reasoning.
analysis is missing.do: Write the analysis once the facts are checked and the lenses are chosen.

is not recorded.what: A decision that is yours to make has not been recorded.
is not recorded.why: The run stops twice for your decision: before the lenses are chosen and before the final report.
is not recorded.do: Answer the open question for this run. The report is built after that.

a decision is recorded as unattended, bu.what: A decision in this run is marked as taken without a person, but the run was not started that way.
a decision is recorded as unattended, bu.why: Only a run started unattended may skip its stops, so this decision cannot be trusted as a person's.
a decision is recorded as unattended, bu.do: Answer the decision again as a person, or start a new run that is unattended from the beginning.

a text that says an amount is missing na.what: A text of the analysis says that no source gives a price, a cost or another amount, while confirmed facts of this run state amounts.
a text that says an amount is missing na.why: A reader would take the amount as missing, while the run holds amounts that may answer it.
a text that says an amount is missing na.do: Name at least one of the listed facts in the text and say why its amount does not answer the point, or change the text.

a not-found entry about money names none.what: The analysis says a price or cost was not found, but confirmed facts state amounts of money (the problem lists them).
a not-found entry about money names none.why: A reader would believe no source gives any figure, while the run holds some; they may answer the question or may not.
a not-found entry about money names none.do: Use those amounts, or name one in the entry and say why it does not answer (F35 is a build budget, not a price). An older run may need this to rebuild.

fact was never settled.what: Fact {id} was proposed but never checked to the end.
fact was never settled.why: Either its quote check or its support check is missing.
fact was never settled.do: Run the checks for {id}, then settle the facts again.

support check not passed.what: The support check for fact {id} has not passed.
support check not passed.why: Either nobody has judged yet whether the quote supports the fact, or the judgement went against it.
support check not passed.do: Run the support check for {id}, then settle the facts again.

status does not follow from the checks.what: The status of fact {id} does not match its checks.
status does not follow from the checks.why: The fact or its checks were changed after the status was set, or the status was changed by hand.
status does not follow from the checks.do: Settle the facts again so that every status follows from its checks.

fact {id} is missing.what: Fact {id} was added to this run but can no longer be found.
fact {id} is missing.why: Its saved entry was deleted or moved. Facts are never removed; a fact that should not count is withdrawn.
fact {id} is missing.do: Restore fact {id} from a backup, or start the run again.

source {id} is missing.what: Source {id} was saved in this run but can no longer be found.
source {id} is missing.why: Its saved entry was deleted or moved after it was saved.
source {id} is missing.do: Restore source {id} from a backup, or start the run again.

run.json is missing.what: This run has lost its basic details.
run.json is missing.why: The details that name the question and the run are not there any more.
run.json is missing.do: Restore the run from a backup, or start the run again.

may not be opened by this user.what: An item of this run is saved, but your user account on this computer may not open it.
may not be opened by this user.why: The setting for who may read the file was changed, often by hand or when the run was copied from another account or computer.
may not be opened by this user.do: Allow your user account to read it again, for example in the run folder's settings for who may read each item, then check the run again.

run.json may not be opened.what: This run's basic details are saved, but your user account on this computer may not open them.
run.json may not be opened.why: The setting for who may read the file was changed, often by hand or when the run was copied from another account or computer.
run.json may not be opened.do: Allow your user account to read them again, for example in the run folder's settings for who may read each item, then check the run again.

not valid JSON.what: A saved item of this run cannot be read.
not valid JSON.why: It is empty or damaged, often after a manual edit or an interrupted save.
not valid JSON.do: Restore it from a backup, or run the step that writes it again.

must not be empty.what: Something the report needs has been left blank.
must not be empty.why: Every source, fact and analysis part has to be filled in before it can be shown.
must not be empty.do: Fill in the blank part, or run the step that writes it again.

in_question is missing; it must be yes o.what: A proposed capacity move does not say whether it falls inside the run's question.
in_question is missing; it must be yes o.why: The answer counts only moves inside the question; whether one is inside is the extractor's judgement, made against the question and checked by the support checker.
in_question is missing; it must be yes o.do: Send the move back to the extractor to propose it again with in_question set to yes or no. Do not decide it yourself.

not an allowed value.what: An entry has a value the program does not recognise.
not an allowed value.why: Only the listed choices can be used there, such as a source type or a confidence level.
not an allowed value.do: Replace it with one of the allowed choices, or run the step that writes it again.

file name does not match id.what: An item is stored under a name that does not match its own number.
file name does not match id.why: It may have been copied or renamed by hand.
file name does not match id.do: Give it back its own number, or add it again as a new item.

non-public source in a public run.what: This run is public, but it contains a source that is not.
non-public source in a public run.why: Licensed and internal sources may only be used in a private run.
non-public source in a public run.do: Start the run again without that source: a public run uses only sources that anyone can read.

provenance is required for non-public so.what: A source that is not public does not say where it came from.
provenance is required for non-public so.why: For licensed and internal material, the report must show who supplied it and on what basis.
provenance is required for non-public so.do: Add who supplied the source and on what basis.

only a saved web page can have the note.what: Source {id} carries the note that its copy holds little running text, but it is not a saved web page.
only a saved web page can have the note.why: The program gives this note only to a web page it saved, so the note was added or changed by hand.
only a saved web page can have the note.do: Take the note out of source {id}, or save the page again as a new source.

source {id} does not exist.what: A fact or source points to source {id}, which is not saved in this run.
source {id} does not exist.why: The source was never saved, or it was removed or renamed.
source {id} does not exist.do: Save source {id}, or point to a source that exists.

based_on must not form a loop.what: Some sources are each said to be based on the others.
based_on must not form a loop.why: A source cannot be based on itself, not even through other sources.
based_on must not form a loop.do: Correct which source is based on which, so that the chain ends at the original.

saved copy is missing.what: The saved copy of a source cannot be found.
saved copy is missing.why: It was deleted or moved after it was saved.
saved copy is missing.do: Save the source again as a new source, add its facts again from the new copy, and take the old facts out of the analysis.

quote must have 5 to 50 words.what: A quote is too short or too long.
quote must have 5 to 50 words.why: A quote is one or two sentences of 5 to 50 words, so that it can be checked and read in context.
quote must have 5 to 50 words.do: Choose one or two sentences from the saved copy and add them as a new fact.

an early signal must be marked tentative.what: A fact is marked as an early signal, but it is not marked tentative.
an early signal must be marked tentative.why: An early signal is a hint, such as a building permit, a job posting or a regulator notice. It is not an announcement, so it can never count as confirmed.
an early signal must be marked tentative.do: This fact was changed outside the program. Mark it tentative by hand, with a line on what kind of hint it is, or start a new run.

an early signal must be a general fact.what: A fact is marked as an early signal, but it describes a capacity move.
an early signal must be a general fact.why: A capacity move is something a company has announced. An early signal is only a hint, and it is shown apart from the announced moves.
an early signal must be a general fact.do: Add the hint again as a new general fact, and withdraw the old one.

a fact from a permit, a job posting or a.what: A fact comes from a building permit, a job posting or a regulator notice, but it is not marked as an early signal.
a fact from a permit, a job posting or a.why: These sources only hint at a move. A hint has to be marked, so that it is shown apart from announced moves and can never count as confirmed.
a fact from a permit, a job posting or a.do: Add the fact again as a new fact marked as an early signal, tentative and general, and withdraw the old one.

a baseline takes its wording from its fa.what: A baseline has wording of its own.
a baseline takes its wording from its fa.why: A baseline shows what its facts say. Wording written next to them could state a figure that none of them supports.
a baseline takes its wording from its fa.do: Take the wording out and name only the facts. The report then shows what each fact says.

chain must have at least one fact step.what: A key message does not name any fact it rests on.
chain must have at least one fact step.why: Each message needs at least one sourced fact in its line of reasoning.
chain must have at least one fact step.do: Add a step that names the supporting fact, or remove the message.

chain must have exactly one conclusion s.what: A key message does not have exactly one conclusion.
chain must have exactly one conclusion s.why: Its line of reasoning has to end in one single conclusion.
chain must have exactly one conclusion s.do: Keep one conclusion step for the message and merge or remove the others.

a fact step must name at least one fact.what: A step of a key message is shown as a fact, but it names no checked fact.
a fact step must name at least one fact.why: The report would print it as a fact with nothing behind it.
a fact step must name at least one fact.do: Name the fact the step rests on, or mark the step as reasoning.

the last step of a chain must be its con.what: A key message has a step after its conclusion.
the last step of a chain must be its con.why: The line of reasoning leads to the conclusion, so a step after it would stand on nothing.
the last step of a chain must be its con.do: Move the conclusion to the end, or put the later step before it.

lens must have exactly 3 questions.what: A lens does not have exactly three questions.
lens must have exactly 3 questions.why: Every lens asks three questions so that the lenses can be compared.
lens must have exactly 3 questions.do: Change the lens to three questions, or choose a different lens.

must have at least one entry.what: A list that needs at least one entry is empty.
must have at least one entry.why: Assumptions, scenarios, signposts and calculations only make sense with something in them.
must have at least one entry.do: Add the missing entry, or remove the empty item.

use no scenarios or between two and four.what: The analysis has the wrong number of scenarios.
use no scenarios or between two and four.why: Scenarios only help when there are two to four of them to compare.
use no scenarios or between two and four.do: Write between two and four scenarios, or none at all.

must be a list.what: A part of the analysis that should hold several entries holds a single value instead.
must be a list.why: The report lists each entry on its own, so the part must be written as a list.
must be a list.do: Write the part as a list of entries, or run the step that writes the analysis again.

must be an object.what: An entry of the analysis is a bare value where the report expects its named parts.
must be an object.why: The report reads each entry by its parts, such as its text and the facts it names.
must be an object.do: Write the entry with its named parts, or run the step that writes the analysis again.

must be text.what: A part that should be text holds something else, such as a number or a list.
must be text.why: Only plain text can be shown and checked there.
must be text.do: Write that part as plain text, or run the step that writes it again.

write the number without thousands separ.what: A size is written with a thousands separator, such as 1.200 or 1,200.
write the number without thousands separ.why: The program cannot tell whether 1.200 means one thousand two hundred or one point two, so it does not guess.
write the number without thousands separ.do: Write the size as a plain number, such as 1200, and add the fact again.

must be a date like 2027-12-31.what: A prediction has no usable date.
must be a date like 2027-12-31.why: The date says by when the prediction can be judged.
must be a date like 2027-12-31.do: Write the date as year, month and day, for example 2027-12-31.

must be a whole number from 1 to 99.what: A prediction has no usable probability.
must be a whole number from 1 to 99.why: A probability is a whole percentage; 0 and 100 would leave no room for doubt.
must be a whole number from 1 to 99.do: Enter a whole number from 1 to 99.

id {id} is used more than once.what: Two items in the analysis share the label {id}.
id {id} is used more than once.why: Each assumption, scenario, prediction and calculation needs its own label so that others can refer to it.
id {id} is used more than once.do: Give one of them a new label.

assumption {id} does not exist.what: A scenario relies on assumption {id}, which does not exist.
assumption {id} does not exist.why: The assumption was removed, renamed or never written.
assumption {id} does not exist.do: Add assumption {id}, or take it out of the scenario.

scenario {id} does not exist.what: A watch item points to scenario {id}, which does not exist.
scenario {id} does not exist.why: The scenario was removed, renamed or never written.
scenario {id} does not exist.do: Point the watch item to an existing scenario, or leave the link out.

message {id} does not exist.what: A prediction belongs to key message {id}, which does not exist.
message {id} does not exist.why: The message was removed, renamed or never written.
message {id} does not exist.do: Point the prediction to an existing message, or remove it.

fact {id} does not exist.what: The analysis uses fact {id}, but there is no such fact in this run.
fact {id} does not exist.why: The fact was never added, or the number is wrong.
fact {id} does not exist.do: Correct the number, or add the fact and check it.

lens {id} does not exist.what: The analysis names the lens {id}, which is not available.
lens {id} does not exist.why: No lens of that name is among the lenses on offer.
lens {id} does not exist.do: Choose one of the available lenses for that note.

input {id} is listed more than once.what: A calculation lists fact {id} more than once.
input {id} is listed more than once.why: It would be counted twice in the total.

input {id} is stated in.what: Fact {id} is stated in a different unit than the calculation uses.
input {id} is stated in.why: The program never converts units, so every figure must be in the unit of the total.
input {id} is stated in.do: Use facts stated in the same unit, or change the unit of the calculation.

input {id} has no plain number.what: Fact {id} does not give its size as a plain number.
input {id} has no plain number.why: The program can only add figures written as plain numbers, such as 2 or 2.5.
input {id} has no plain number.do: Use a fact whose size is a plain number, or leave {id} out.

input {id} is not a settled capacity mov.what: A calculation uses {id}, which is not a settled capacity move.
input {id} is not a settled capacity mov.why: Only confirmed or uncertain capacity moves can be added up.
input {id} is not a settled capacity mov.do: Use settled capacity moves only, or finish checking {id} first.

share inputs must be part of the whole.what: A share is worked out from facts that are not part of the whole.
share inputs must be part of the whole.why: A share compares a part with the total it belongs to.
share inputs must be part of the whole.do: Add the parts to the list of facts that make up the whole.

whole is zero.what: A share cannot be worked out because the whole adds up to zero.
whole is zero.why: A share of nothing has no meaning.
whole is zero.do: Check the facts that make up the whole, or leave the share out.

operation is not an allowed value.what: A calculation asks for something the program cannot do.
operation is not an allowed value.why: The program can add up, count and work out a share.
operation is not an allowed value.do: Choose one of these three: sum, count or share.

of_fact_ids must be a list.what: A share does not list the facts that make up its whole.
of_fact_ids must be a list.why: The facts that form the whole have to be given as a list.
of_fact_ids must be a list.do: List the facts that make up the whole.

fact_ids must be a list.what: A calculation does not list the facts it is built from.
fact_ids must be a list.why: The facts have to be given as a list so that each one can be checked.
fact_ids must be a list.do: List the facts that the calculation is built from.

unit is required.what: A total or share has no unit.
unit is required.why: Figures can only be added when a unit says what they count, such as lines or tonnes.
unit is required.do: State the unit that all the figures use.

numbers are too large to calculate exact.what: The figures in a calculation are too large to add exactly.
numbers are too large to calculate exact.why: The program refuses to round a total.
numbers are too large to calculate exact.do: Check the figures for a typing error, or split the calculation.

the pack cannot be read.what: The company pack cannot be read.
the pack cannot be read.why: The file is empty or damaged, often after a manual edit, so it no longer holds a set of named settings that can be read.
the pack cannot be read.do: Restore the pack from a backup, or start again from the demo pack.

the pack is nested too deeply to read.what: The company pack has too many parts inside other parts to be read.
the pack is nested too deeply to read.why: A manual edit may have left brackets open, or repeated a block many times.
the pack is nested too deeply to read.do: Remove the extra brackets, or start again from the demo pack.

the pack must be a set of named settings.what: The company pack is not written as a set of named settings.
the pack must be a set of named settings.why: A pack holds settings such as company, industry and places, each with its own name.
the pack must be a set of named settings.do: Write the pack the way the demo pack is written.

must be a whole number from 1 to 120.what: The time window in the pack is not a whole number of months from 1 to 120.
must be a whole number from 1 to 120.why: The window sets how far back the program looks for sources. Without one it uses 36 months.
must be a whole number from 1 to 120.do: Write a whole number from 1 to 120, or remove the setting to use 36 months.

a pack lists candidates only.what: A competitor or watched company in the pack is not marked as a candidate.
a pack lists candidates only.why: A pack holds pointers, not facts. A company stays a candidate until a source confirms what it does.
a pack lists candidates only.do: Set the status to candidate. Facts about the company come from sources, not from the pack.

a question framed by the user must say w.what: A question in the pack that is framed by the user does not say who framed it.
a question framed by the user must say w.why: Anyone who reads the results needs to know whose question it is.
a question framed by the user must say w.do: Say who framed the question, such as the name of a person or a team.

a pack setting must not be left empty.what: In the pack, {field} is blank or missing.
a pack setting must not be left empty.why: The program needs it to describe the company, its question or where to look.
a pack setting must not be left empty.do: Fill in {field}, or add it to the pack.

a pack list needs at least one entry.what: In the pack, {field} is an empty list, but it needs at least one entry.
a pack list needs at least one entry.why: A pack needs at least one strategic question, one place to look and one language.

a pack setting must be a list.what: In the pack, {field} should be a list, but it is missing or holds a single value.
a pack setting must be a list.why: Each entry is read on its own, so a single value cannot stand in for a list.
a pack setting must be a list.do: Write {field} as a list, even with one entry. Only competitors, watch, units, demand drivers, vocabulary and other names may be empty or left out.

a pack list entry must be text.what: In the pack, {field} is not plain text.
a pack list entry must be text.why: Units, demand drivers and languages are plain words, so numbers or nested parts cannot be used there.

a pack entry must be a set of named sett.what: In the pack, {field} is not written as a set of named settings.
a pack entry must be a set of named sett.why: A question, competitor, place or term needs named parts, such as a name and a web address.
a pack entry must be a set of named sett.do: Rewrite {field} the way the demo pack writes its entries.

the pack has a setting that is not known.what: The program does not recognise {field} in the pack.
the pack has a setting that is not known.why: The name may be misspelt, and a misspelt setting would otherwise be ignored without a warning.
the pack has a setting that is not known.do: Correct the name of {field}, or remove it from the pack.

the pack's id may use only lower-case le.what: The pack's id is missing or is not written in the allowed way.
the pack's id may use only lower-case le.why: The id is also the name the pack is saved under, so it can use only lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.
the pack's id may use only lower-case le.do: Change the id to lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, with no hyphen at the start or end, such as my-company.

the pack's file name does not match its.what: The name the pack is saved under does not match its id.
the pack's file name does not match its.why: The id was changed, or the pack file was copied or renamed by hand.
the pack's file name does not match its.do: The pack file must be named the id followed by .json. Rename it, or change the id to match its name.

a question's framing must be company or.what: The framing of a question in the pack is missing or not allowed.
a question's framing must be company or.why: The framing says whether the question comes from the company's own statements or from the person who framed it.
a question's framing must be company or.do: Write company for a question taken from the company, or user for a question framed by a person.

who suggested a name must be user or sea.what: A competitor or watched company in the pack does not say who suggested it, or says it wrongly.
who suggested a name must be user or sea.why: The pack must show whether a person or a search put the name on the list.
who suggested a name must be user or sea.do: Write user if a person suggested the name, or search if a search found it.

the illustrative mark must be true or fa.what: The pack does not say clearly whether it is illustrative.
the illustrative mark must be true or fa.why: Readers must be able to tell invented practice material from a real pack.
the illustrative mark must be true or fa.do: Write true for practice material with invented companies, or false for a real company pack.

the screening mark must be true or false.what: The pack does not say clearly whether it is for screening a startup.
the screening mark must be true or false.why: A screening run writes a memo on one startup, so the run must know which kind it is.
the screening mark must be true or false.do: Write true for a pack on a startup to screen, or leave the setting out for a company pack.

the kind of a place to look is not one t.what: A place to look in the pack has a kind that is missing or not allowed.
the kind of a place to look is not one t.why: The kind tells the search what sort of source to expect there.
the kind of a place to look is not one t.do: Use one of these kinds: investor_relations, press_room, filings, annual_reports, regulator, trade_press, permits or job_postings.

a place to look needs a web address star.what: A place to look in the pack has no usable web address.
a place to look needs a web address star.why: The program needs an address it can open, and a password in the address would be stored in the pack for anyone to read.
a place to look needs a web address star.do: Write an address starting with http or https and holding no user name or password.

a name found by search needs the address.what: A name in the pack that was found by search does not give a usable address where it was found.
a name found by search needs the address.why: Without the address, nobody can check why the name is on the list.
a name found by search needs the address.do: Add a web address starting with http or https, with no user name or password, or mark the name as suggested by the user.

a question taken from the company needs.what: A question in the pack that is taken from the company's own statements has no usable quote and address.
a question taken from the company needs.why: A pack never claims what a company says. It points to a quote that will be checked, at an address with no user name or password.
a question taken from the company needs.do: Add a quote of 5 to 50 words and a web address starting with http or https, or mark the question as framed by the user.

an evidence address needs a web address.what: An address given as evidence for a question in the pack is not usable.
an evidence address needs a web address.why: The program needs an address it can open, and a password in the address would be stored in the pack for anyone to read.
an evidence address needs a web address.do: Use an address starting with http or https and holding no user name or password, or leave the evidence out.

This is the invented practice run, so it.what: The document was not added, because this run is the invented practice run.
This is the invented practice run, so it.why: The practice run was built by the demo command. Its private-mode notice was never shown to a person, so it cannot take real non-public material.
This is the invented practice run, so it.do: Start a new run to work with your own material.

the practice-run mark is only allowed on.what: This run is marked as the invented practice run, but it is not one.
the practice-run mark is only allowed on.why: Only the private practice run that the demo command builds may carry that mark. The mark was added by hand, or the run was changed afterwards.
the practice-run mark is only allowed on.do: Build the practice run again with the demo command, or start a new run for your own material.

a capacity move names its company in fie.what: A capacity move names its company a second time, as the company the fact is about.
a capacity move names its company in fie.why: A capacity move keeps its company with the other details of the move. A second place for it could name a different company.
a capacity move names its company in fie.do: Leave out the company the fact is about on a capacity move, and keep the company with the details of the move.

a connection that names no party must de.what: A fact lists a customer, buyer, seller or partner without a name and without a description.
a connection that names no party must de.why: A party the source does not name is shown by the words the source uses for it. Without them the report cannot say who is meant.
a connection that names no party must de.do: Copy the source's words for the party into description, or give its name in party.

a connection names its other party; leav.what: A proposed fact lists a customer, buyer, seller or partner without naming it.
a connection names its other party; leav.why: A tie with no named party tells the reader nothing they can follow up. The fact's statement can still say that the source mentions an unnamed party.
a connection names its other party; leav.do: Name the party in party, or leave the connection out and let the statement say it.

at most one company of a run is its own.what: The run's list of companies marks more than one company as the company the report is for.
at most one company of a run is its own.why: A report is written for one company. With two, the report cannot tell which one is meant.
at most one company of a run is its own.do: Keep the mark on one company and take it off the others, or start the run again from its pack.

a public run may not be compared with a.what: This public run is compared with an earlier run that holds material that is not public.
a public run may not be compared with a.why: The comparison would copy that material into the report of this run, which is meant to be shared.
a public run may not be compared with a.do: Compare it with an earlier public run instead, or build this report without the comparison.

an illustrative run cannot be compared w.what: One of the two runs is invented for illustration and the other is not.
an illustrative run cannot be compared w.why: Invented figures would appear as real ones, or real figures in a report marked as invented.
an illustrative run cannot be compared w.do: Compare two real runs with each other, or two illustrative runs.

the comparison was made for another run.what: The comparison with an earlier run was made for another run and copied into this one.
the comparison was made for another run.why: Its values belong to that other run, so they may not appear in the report of this run.
the comparison was made for another run.do: Run the comparison again, with this run as the current run.

the comparison was made by an earlier ve.what: The comparison with the earlier run was made by an earlier version of the program.
the comparison was made by an earlier ve.why: It does not say whether the earlier run was invented for illustration, so the program cannot check that it fits this run.
the comparison was made by an earlier ve.do: Run the comparison with the earlier run again.

input {id} has changed since the facts w.what: Fact {id} has changed since the facts were last settled, so its status may be out of date.
input {id} has changed since the facts w.why: It was withdrawn, given a new verdict, or one of its sources was linked to another. A total may only use a status that still holds.
input {id} has changed since the facts w.do: Settle the facts, then calculate again.

a baseline may not rest on {id}, an earl.what: The baseline of a competitor rests on {id}, which is an early signal.
a baseline may not rest on {id}, an earl.why: A baseline describes what a company already has. An early signal only hints at a move and is never confirmed.
a baseline may not rest on {id}, an earl.do: Take {id} out of the baseline. Early signals are shown in a block of their own.

the key {id} is set by the program, not.what: A proposed fact sets {id}, which only the program sets.
the key {id} is set by the program, not.why: The program sets it itself, so the value in the proposal would have been dropped without a word.
the key {id} is set by the program, not.do: Leave {id} out and propose the fact again.

the key {id} is not known.what: A fact holds a part called {id} that the program does not know.
the key {id} is not known.why: The name may be misspelt, or the part belongs somewhere else. The program would otherwise ignore it without a word.
the key {id} is not known.do: This fact was changed outside the program. Correct it by hand, or start a new run.

the key {id} is not known in a flag.what: A flag of the look for bias holds a part called {id} that the program does not know.
the key {id} is not known in a flag.why: A flag is a check, a text and the messages it is about, and the report prints nothing else of it.
the key {id} is not known in a flag.do: Have the look for bias done again, and copy only the check, the text and the messages of each flag.

a flag names fact {id}, which does not e.what: A flag of the look for bias names fact {id}, but there is no such fact in this run.
a flag names fact {id}, which does not e.why: A reader would look for a fact that is not there, and a flag is never changed by hand.
a flag names fact {id}, which does not e.do: Have the look for bias done again, so that its flags name only facts of this run.

a flag names message {id}, which does no.what: A flag of the look for bias names message {id}, but there is no such message in this analysis.
a flag names message {id}, which does no.why: The report puts each flag under the messages it is about, and a message that is not there has no place for it.
a flag names message {id}, which does no.do: A message was dropped, so the audit no longer fits. Set the audit's list of findings back to the empty list, and do the look for bias again.

write the size as text, such as \"2.5\".what: The size of a capacity move is written as a bare number, not as text.
write the size as text, such as \"2.5\".why: Sizes are kept exactly as written, so that 2.50 stays 2.50, and only text keeps them that way.
write the size as text, such as \"2.5\".do: This fact was changed outside the program. Write its size by hand as text, such as "2.5", or start a new run.

the practice run can only be compared wi.what: This is the invented practice run, and the earlier run is not a practice run.
the practice run can only be compared wi.why: The practice run takes no material from outside the practice, so it takes no values from another run either.
the practice run can only be compared wi.do: Compare it with another practice run built with the demo command, or compare runs of your own.

no lens files.why: Thinking lenses are chosen from this folder, so a folder without any offers nothing to choose.
no lens files.do: Give the folder that holds the lenses, or add a lens to it.

a lens id may use only letters, digits,.what: The id of a lens is missing or uses a character that is not allowed.
a lens id may use only letters, digits,.why: The id is also the name the lens is saved under, so it may use only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores.
a lens id may use only letters, digits,.do: Write the id with letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only, such as firm-boundaries, and save the lens under that name.

a lens id must match the name the lens i.what: A lens is saved under a name that differs from its id.
a lens id must match the name the lens i.why: The program finds a lens by its id, so the two must be the same. The lens was renamed, or its id was changed by hand.
a lens id must match the name the lens i.do: Save the lens under its id, or change the id to the name it is saved under.

a lens holds a part that the program doe.what: The program does not recognise {field} in the lens.
a lens holds a part that the program doe.why: The name may be misspelt, or text was added that does not belong in a lens. A part the program does not know would otherwise be ignored without a warning.
a lens holds a part that the program doe.do: Correct the name of {field}, or remove it from the lens.

a lens part must be filled in with text.what: In the lens, {field} is blank, missing or not plain text.
a lens part must be filled in with text.why: The lens file holds every part of a lens, so each one needs its own words.
a lens part must be filled in with text.do: Write {field} as plain text, in your own words.

a lens text may be at most 400 character.what: In the lens, {field} is longer than 400 characters.
a lens text may be at most 400 character.why: A lens says its idea in a few short sentences of its own. A long text may hold a passage copied from the original, which must not be shipped.
a lens text may be at most 400 character.do: Shorten {field} to at most 400 characters, in your own words.

a lens needs at least one original.what: The lens names no original that it rests on.
a lens needs at least one original.why: Anyone who uses a lens must be able to see which work or course it comes from, and how closely that was checked.
a lens needs at least one original.do: Add at least one original with its reference, its level and its link, the way the demo lenses do.

an original of a lens needs its referenc.what: In the lens, {field} is not written with a reference, a level and a link.
an original of a lens needs its referenc.why: Each original says which work the lens rests on, how closely it was checked and where a reader can find it.
an original of a lens needs its referenc.do: Write {field} the way the demo lenses write their originals.

a lens link must be none or a web addres.what: In the lens, {field} is not a usable link.
a lens link must be none or a web addres.why: A link must open for a reader: it starts with http or https, has a port from 1 to 65535 if any, and holds no user name, password, space or hidden character.
a lens link must be none or a web addres.do: Write the address in that form, with a site name of plain letters a to z, digits, hyphens and dots, or set the link to none, as the demo lenses do.

a lens for real use must say when it was.what: A lens that is meant to ship does not say on which day it was checked.
a lens for real use must say when it was.why: A lens that ships with the plugin keeps in its file the day its statements were last checked against its originals.
a lens for real use must say when it was.do: Add the day the lens was checked, written as year, month and day, such as 2026-11-15.

the day a lens was checked must be writt.what: The day the lens was checked is not a usable date.
the day a lens was checked must be writt.why: The day is written as year, month and day, so that anyone can tell how recent the check of the lens is.
the day a lens was checked must be writt.do: Write the day as year, month and day, such as 2026-11-15.

the day a lens was checked lies in the f.what: The day the lens was checked lies in the future.
the day a lens was checked lies in the f.why: A lens can only name the day of a check that has taken place. A later date is a typing error.
the day a lens was checked lies in the f.do: Write the day on which the lens was really checked.

a lens for real use may not rest on an i.what: A lens that is meant to ship names an invented reference as its original.
a lens for real use may not rest on an i.why: A reference that begins with the word Illustrative belongs to an invented practice lens, which may not be shipped as a real one.
a lens for real use may not rest on an i.do: Name the real work or course the lens rests on, or keep the lens as practice material.

a lens cannot be read.why: It is empty, damaged, nested too deeply, not one set of named parts, saved in another text format, or a folder. Or your user account may not open it.
a lens cannot be read.do: Restore the lens from a backup, or start again from a copy of a demo lens. If it is locked, allow your user account to read it.

a lens level must be original_read, cour.what: In the lens, {field} is missing or not one of the four levels.
a lens level must be original_read, cour.why: The level says how closely the original was checked, from original_read, the work itself, down to reference_confirmed, its reference only. The levels between are course_slides and secondary_source_read.
a lens level must be original_read, cour.do: Write original_read, course_slides, secondary_source_read or reference_confirmed, and never a higher level than the check reached.

a lens entry read as a source about a wo.why: An entry whose level says that a source about the work was read must say which work the source is about, so that nobody takes the source for the work.
a lens entry read as a source about a wo.do: Write in {field} the work that the source is about, in plain words.

only a lens entry read as a source about.what: In the lens, {field} stands in an entry that is not read as a source about a work.
only a lens entry read as a source about.why: Only an entry whose level is secondary_source_read has a work that it is about. Anywhere else the part would be ignored without a warning.
only a lens entry read as a source about.do: Remove {field}, or change the level of the entry to secondary_source_read if a source about the work was read.

a shipped lens entry at the level refere.what: In the lens, {field} is not a web address.
a shipped lens entry at the level refere.why: Its text was not read, so a reader must be able to find the work itself and read further.
a shipped lens entry at the level refere.do: Write the web address of the page that confirms the work, starting with http or https.

a lens entry read as a source about a wo.what: In the lens, {field} is not a web address.
a lens entry read as a source about a wo.why: A source that stands in for the work must be one that anyone can open and confirm, so its link may not be none.
a lens entry read as a source about a wo.do: Write the web address of the source that was read, starting with http or https.

the lens folder cannot be read.what: The lens folder, or a name in it, cannot be opened.
the lens folder cannot be read.why: Your user account may not list the folder, or may list it but not open the files in it.
the lens folder cannot be read.do: Allow your user account to read and open the lens folder, then check the lenses again.

the lens folder for real use needs a the.what: The lens folder has no list that sorts its lenses into themes.
the lens folder for real use needs a the.why: The lenses that ship are offered grouped by theme, and the grouping is read from one list kept in the lens folder.
the lens folder for real use needs a the.do: Add the list of themes to the lens folder, with each lens in exactly one theme.

the themes index of the lenses cannot be.what: The themes index of the lenses cannot be read.
the themes index of the lenses cannot be.why: It is empty, damaged, nested too deeply, not one set of named parts, saved in another text format, or a folder. Or your user account may not open it.
the themes index of the lenses cannot be.do: Write the list of themes again, each theme with a name and its lens ids.

the themes index of the lenses holds a p.what: The program does not recognise {field} in the themes index of the lenses.
the themes index of the lenses holds a p.why: The name may be misspelt, or text was added that does not belong in the index. A part the program does not know would otherwise be ignored without a warning.
the themes index of the lenses holds a p.do: Correct the name of {field}, or remove it from the index.

the themes index of the lenses must hold.what: In the themes index of the lenses, {field} is missing or is not a list.
the themes index of the lenses must hold.why: The index holds one list of themes, and each theme holds the lenses it groups.
the themes index of the lenses must hold.do: Write {field} as a list of themes, each with a name and a list of lens ids.

a theme of the lenses needs a name and a.what: In the themes index of the lenses, {field} is not written as a name and a list of lens ids.
a theme of the lenses needs a name and a.why: Each theme groups lenses under a name, and a lens id is plain text.
a theme of the lenses needs a name and a.do: Write {field} the way the other themes are written: a name, and the lens ids in a list.

a theme of the lenses needs a name of at.what: In the themes index of the lenses, {field} is blank, missing, not plain text or longer than 400 characters.
a theme of the lenses needs a name of at.why: A theme is offered under its name, and a short name keeps every theme easy to read.
a theme of the lenses needs a name of at.do: Write a short name for the theme in {field}, in plain text.

a theme of the lenses names a lens that.what: In the themes index of the lenses, {field} names a lens that is not in the lens folder.
a theme of the lenses names a lens that.why: The id may be misspelt or written in another case than the lens is named, or the lens may have been removed or renamed.
a theme of the lenses names a lens that.do: Write the id exactly as the lens is named in the lens folder, or remove it from the theme.

a lens may be listed only once in the th.what: In the themes index of the lenses, {field} names a lens that is already listed.
a lens may be listed only once in the th.why: Each lens belongs to exactly one theme, so that it is offered once.
a lens may be listed only once in the th.do: Keep the lens in one theme and remove it from the other.

a lens for real use must be in one theme.what: The lens is in no theme of the themes index.
a lens for real use must be in one theme.why: Every lens that ships is offered under a theme, so a lens that is in none would be left unsorted.
a lens for real use must be in one theme.do: Add the lens id to one theme in the list of themes, or add a new theme for it.

a lens recommendation may name at most 4.what: The lens advisor suggested more than four lenses.
a lens recommendation may name at most 4.why: A short list keeps the first stop easy to read, and the person can still pick any lens from the full list.
a lens recommendation may name at most 4.do: Keep the four lenses that fit the question best, and suggest the list again.

a lens recommendation that names no lens.what: The lens advisor suggested no lens but did not say why.
a lens recommendation that names no lens.why: An empty list is allowed, but the person needs the reason to judge it.
a lens recommendation that names no lens.do: Add a note that says in a sentence why no lens fits the question, and suggest the list again.

the lens recommendation must hold a list.what: The lens suggestion does not hold a list of lenses.
the lens recommendation must hold a list.why: The program can only check and keep a list, one lens after another in the order of their rank.
the lens recommendation must hold a list.do: Send the suggestion again with its lenses as a list, which may be empty.

an entry of the lens recommendation must.what: A suggested lens does not hold exactly its five parts.
an entry of the lens recommendation must.why: Each suggestion names the lens, the part of the question, why it fits, the facts it could use and what it lacks, and nothing else.
an entry of the lens recommendation must.do: Give each suggested lens exactly those five parts, and suggest the list again.

an entry of the lens recommendation name.what: A suggested lens is not in the lens folder of this run.
an entry of the lens recommendation name.why: Only a lens that the program can read and check may be suggested to the person.
an entry of the lens recommendation name.do: Use the exact name of a lens from the list of lenses, and suggest the list again.

an entry of the lens recommendation name.what: A suggested lens fails the lens check.
an entry of the lens recommendation name.why: A lens with a missing or broken part cannot be offered to the person as a choice.
an entry of the lens recommendation name.do: Suggest another lens, or repair that lens and check the lens folder again.

the lens recommendation names a lens twi.what: The same lens is suggested twice.
the lens recommendation names a lens twi.why: Each lens may stand in the list once, so that its place in the ranking is clear.
the lens recommendation names a lens twi.do: Keep the lens once, where it ranks best, and suggest the list again.

the part of the question in a lens recom.what: The part of the question named for a lens is shorter than 2 words or longer than 15.
the part of the question in a lens recom.why: A short, exact part shows which words of the question the lens is about.
the part of the question in a lens recom.do: Copy between 2 and 15 words from the question, and suggest the list again.

the part of the question in a lens recom.what: The part of the question named for a lens is not in the question word for word.
the part of the question in a lens recom.why: Only capital letters and spacing may differ, so a word cut in half or changed does not count as a copy.
the part of the question in a lens recom.do: Copy the words exactly as the question has them, and suggest the list again.

the facts of an entry of the lens recomm.what: The facts named for a suggested lens are not a list of fact numbers.
the facts of an entry of the lens recomm.why: The program checks each named fact on its own, so the facts come as a list, which may be empty.
the facts of an entry of the lens recomm.do: Name the facts as a list of numbers such as F2, and suggest the list again.

the lens recommendation names a fact num.what: A suggested lens names a fact number that this run does not have.
the lens recommendation names a fact num.why: Only facts of this run may stand behind a suggestion.
the lens recommendation names a fact num.do: Use the numbers of the facts that count, as the lens advisor was shown them, and suggest the list again.

the lens recommendation names a fact tha.what: A suggested lens names a fact that does not count.
the lens recommendation names a fact tha.why: A rejected, withdrawn or unchecked fact may not stand behind a suggestion, just as it may not stand behind the report.
the lens recommendation names a fact tha.do: Leave that fact out or name one that counts, and suggest the list again.

a text of the lens recommendation must b.what: A text of the lens suggestion is empty or is not text.
a text of the lens recommendation must b.why: Every part that the person reads must say something.
a text of the lens recommendation must b.do: Fill in the text, and suggest the list again.

a text of the lens recommendation may be.what: A text of the lens suggestion is longer than 400 characters.
a text of the lens recommendation may be.why: Short texts keep the first stop easy to read.
a text of the lens recommendation may be.do: Shorten the text, and suggest the list again.

only the lens advisor may record the len.what: Someone other than the lens advisor tried to keep a lens suggestion.
only the lens advisor may record the len.why: Only the lens advisor makes the suggestion, so the person always knows where it came from.
only the lens advisor may record the len.do: Let the lens advisor make the suggestion. It is never written by another helper or by hand.

the lens recommendation was refused beca.what: The lens suggestion was not kept because it does not pass the form check.
the lens recommendation was refused beca.why: Each problem it has is named on its own.
the lens recommendation was refused beca.do: Fix each named problem, and suggest the list again.

the saved lens recommendation does not h.what: The saved lens suggestion of this run lacks a part, or holds a part that the program does not write.
the saved lens recommendation does not h.why: It was changed after the program wrote it, so it can no longer be shown as it was made.
the saved lens recommendation does not h.do: It does not stop the report or the run. Nothing is repaired: the list is only advice, so what can still be read is shown, each changed part marked where it stands.

a part of the saved lens recommendation.what: A part of the saved lens suggestion of this run has the wrong form.
a part of the saved lens recommendation.why: It was changed after the program wrote it, so it can no longer be shown as it was made.
a part of the saved lens recommendation.do: It does not stop the report or the run. Nothing is repaired: the list is only advice, so what can still be read is shown, each changed part marked where it stands.

a reader's note on a link of the saved l.what: A second reader's note on a link of the saved lens suggestion is longer than 2,000 characters.
a reader's note on a link of the saved l.why: A note is one to three sentences, so a longer one was changed after the program wrote it.
a reader's note on a link of the saved l.do: It does not stop the report or the run. Nothing is repaired: the list is only advice, so what can still be read is shown, each changed part marked where it stands.

an entry of the lens recommendation name.what: A suggested lens names the same fact twice.
an entry of the lens recommendation name.why: Each fact stands behind a lens once, so that each link between them is read once.
an entry of the lens recommendation name.do: Name the fact once, and suggest the list again.

only a link reader may record a verdict.what: Someone other than a link reader tried to give a verdict on a suggested link.
only a link reader may record a verdict.why: Only the two readers judge a link, so that each verdict is known to be theirs.
only a link reader may record a verdict.do: Let a link reader give its own verdict. A verdict is never written by another helper or by hand.

a link reader named a link that the lens.what: A link reader named a lens and a fact that the lens suggestion does not tie together.
a link reader named a link that the lens.why: A reader judges only the links the lens advisor suggested.
a link reader named a link that the lens.do: Name the lens and the fact exactly as the reader was given them.

this run holds no lens recommendation th.what: The run has no readable lens suggestion for a link reader to judge.
this run holds no lens recommendation th.why: A verdict belongs to a link of a suggestion, so without one there is nothing to attach it to.
this run holds no lens recommendation th.do: Let the lens advisor suggest the list first, then let the readers read its links.

a link reader's verdict must be that the.what: A link reader's verdict was neither that the fact bears on the lens nor that it is in doubt.
a link reader's verdict must be that the.why: Only those two verdicts can be counted, so each link ends with a clear mark or none.
a link reader's verdict must be that the.do: Give the verdict again with one of the two allowed verdicts. If the link is unclear, give a doubt.

a link reader that doubts a link must sa.what: A link reader doubted a link but gave no note.
a link reader that doubts a link must sa.why: The person sees the note beside the mark, and a doubt without a reason cannot be weighed.
a link reader that doubts a link must sa.do: Give the verdict again with one sentence that says what the fact does not answer.

a link reader's note may be at most 2,00.what: A link reader's note is longer than 2,000 characters.
a link reader's note may be at most 2,00.why: A note is one to three sentences, so that the person can read it at a glance.
a link reader's note may be at most 2,00.do: Shorten the note, and give the verdict again.

only the project grouper may record the.what: Someone other than the project grouper tried to keep a grouping of the moves into projects.
only the project grouper may record the.why: Only the project grouper groups the moves, so the person always knows where a project came from.
only the project grouper may record the.do: Let the project grouper group the moves. A grouping is never written by another helper or by hand.

a project names a fact that is not a cap.what: A project names fact {field}, which is not a confirmed or uncertain move to add capacity.
a project names a fact that is not a cap.why: A project gathers the reports of one plan, so only moves that count may sit in it.
a project names a fact that is not a cap.do: Take that fact out of the project, check the fact numbers, and group the moves again.

the projects leave out a capacity move t.what: Fact {field}, a confirmed or uncertain move to add capacity, sits in no project.
the projects leave out a capacity move t.why: The report shows every move inside a project, so a move left out would be lost from view.
the projects leave out a capacity move t.do: Put the move into the project it belongs to, or into a project of its own, and group the moves again.

the projects name the same fact twice.what: Fact {field} is named twice in the projects.
the projects name the same fact twice.why: Each move belongs to one project only, or it would be counted twice.
the projects name the same fact twice.do: Keep the fact in the one project it belongs to, and group the moves again.

a project holds moves of more than one c.what: One project holds moves of two different companies.
a project holds moves of more than one c.why: A project is one company's plan, and two spellings of one name already count as one company.
a project holds moves of more than one c.do: Split the project so that each holds the moves of one company, and group the moves again.

a project holds moves in different count.what: The moves of one project name different countries.
a project holds moves in different count.why: A project is one plan at one place. A move that names no country does not count against this.
a project holds moves in different count.do: Split the project by country, and group the moves again.

a project needs a name of at most 120 ch.what: A project has no name, or its name is longer than 120 characters.
a project needs a name of at most 120 ch.why: The report shows each project under its name, so the name must be there and short.
a project needs a name of at most 120 ch.do: Give the project a short name, such as the company and the site, and group the moves again.

the saved projects do not hold exactly t.what: The saved grouping of the moves into projects was changed by hand or is damaged.
the saved projects do not hold exactly t.why: The report can only show projects in the form the program writes. Until then it shows each move on its own.
the saved projects do not hold exactly t.do: Let the project grouper group the moves again. Its new grouping replaces the damaged one.

no such part.what: A part of the helper's input was asked for that is not there.
no such part.why: The input comes in parts so that each one can be read whole, and part 1 says how many parts there are.
no such part.do: Ask for a part from 1 up to the number that part 1 gives under parts.

no saved answer for source.what: A source of this round has no saved answer from its extractor.
no saved answer for source.why: Only saved answers can be joined, and nothing is joined while one is missing.
no saved answer for source.do: Save the reading helper's answer for that source, or leave the source out, and join again.

the saved answer is not an extractor's a.what: A saved answer does not hold a list of proposals.
the saved answer is not an extractor's a.why: It must be the reading helper's answer as it came, with its proposals and its notes.
the saved answer is not an extractor's a.do: Ask the reading helper once more, save its answer unchanged, and join again.

no such proposal.what: A merge names a proposal that is not there.
no such proposal.why: A proposal is named by its source and its place in that source's proposals, counted from 1, and only sources of this round count.
no such proposal.do: Correct the name in the list of merges, and join again.

a proposal is named twice in the merges.what: One proposal is named in two places of the merges.
a proposal is named twice in the merges.why: A proposal is either kept or folded into one other proposal, never both and never twice.
a proposal is named twice in the merges.do: Name it once in the list of merges, and join again.

a proposal is folded into itself.what: A merge folds a proposal into itself.
a proposal is folded into itself.why: A fold adds the quote of another proposal; a proposal cannot support itself.
a proposal is folded into itself.do: Take it out of its own merge, and join again.

two proposals of one source are in one g.what: A group of the claim matcher holds two proposals of the same source.
two proposals of one source are in one g.why: A group joins what different sources say about one claim; one source cannot confirm itself.
two proposals of one source are in one g.do: Keep one proposal of each source in the group, and send the groups again.

an early signal is in a group.what: A group holds an early signal, as the proposal that stays or as one that folds.
an early signal is in a group.why: An early signal, such as a permit or a job posting, is never confirmed and never confirms another fact.
an early signal is in a group.do: Take the early signal out of the group, and send the groups again.

capacity moves of different companies ar.what: A group holds capacity moves of different companies.
capacity moves of different companies ar.why: Proposals of one group must state the same claim, and a move of one company is not a move of another.
capacity moves of different companies ar.do: Group only moves of one company, and send the groups again.

capacity moves in one group state a diff.what: The capacity moves of a group state a different size, unit or announcement date.
capacity moves in one group state a diff.why: Proposals of one group must state the same claim, and moves that differ in what both state are not one move.
capacity moves in one group state a diff.do: Group only moves that agree where both state a value, and send the groups again.

a capacity move in a group names no comp.what: A group holds a capacity move that names no company.
a capacity move in a group names no comp.why: Without a company it cannot be told whether the moves of the group are one move.
a capacity move in a group names no comp.do: Take that move out of the group, and send the groups again.
